sections.title: Lesson 10: Retrieval systems, guests, and project synthesis

keyTerms.definition: Unit 10 of CS229S, covering retrieval, guest evidence, and project synthesis.
The evidence label on every lesson claim, here PLANNED with source attribution pending.

recall.question: What unit and sessions anchor this lesson?
recall.answer: Unit cs229s-U10, concepts C01 to C12, calendar-anchored to Dec 02 (Efficient Retrieval Systems), the Nov 22 Gu and Nov 11 Patel guest lectures, and the project milestones (Oct 21, Nov 11, Dec 06, Dec 09).

keyTerms.definition: The index: expensive to compile, cheap to consult.
Amortized cost at N queries.
Break-even queries vs brute force at 50 ms/query.

recall.question: Write the amortization formula.
recall.answer: Amortized cost at N queries: B/N + q.

recall.question: Build 7200 s once, query 0.005 s. Amortized cost at 1M queries? Break-even N vs 50 ms brute force?
recall.answer: 12.2 ms at 1M queries. Break-even at 160,000 queries.

recall.question: The index never pays off. What is the query volume?
recall.answer: Too low: a corpus queried 10 times a day never earns its index.

keyTerms.definition: PQ: 64 bytes per vector, tiny footprint, unpacking cost at query time.
PQ bytes per vector: storage = docs * code_bytes.
The dense/PQ storage ratio on the toy.

recall.question: Write both storage formulas.
recall.answer: Dense = docs * dims * bytes_float. PQ = docs * code_bytes.

recall.question: 1M docs, 768 dims, fp32 vs 64-byte PQ. Byte counts and ratio?
Recall collapses after compression. What was overdone?
recall.answer: The PQ: too few bytes per vector on a hard distractor set.

keyTerms.definition: ANN: IVF jumps to the right section, HNSW walks a highway of shortcuts.
Fraction of true top-k found.
The toy recall floor: only brute and HNSW qualify.

recall.question: Define recall@k.
recall.answer: Recall@k: fraction of true top-k found.

recall.question: Brute 1.00 @ 50 ms, IVF 0.95 @ 5 ms, HNSW 0.98 @ 8 ms. Which meet a 0.97 floor, at what latencies?
recall.answer: Brute (50 ms) and HNSW (8 ms). IVF fails the floor.

recall.question: Mean recall is fine but users complain. What do you measure?
recall.answer: Recall per query difficulty: mean 0.97 can hide a 0.70 tail on hard queries.

keyTerms.definition: BM25 heard the words, dense got the meaning.
Reciprocal rank fusion: RRF(d) = sum 1/(k + rank).
Two mid ranks beat one top plus one deep rank.

recall.question: Write the RRF formula.
recall.answer: RRF(d) = sum over systems of 1/(k + rank), k = 60.

recall.question: Doc D ranks 3rd and 5th, k=60. Score? Vs a doc ranked 1st and 100th?
Fusion hurts on keyword queries. Why?
recall.answer: The dense list dilutes the BM25 signal where keywords decide.

keyTerms.definition: The cascade: the fast lane screens everyone, the slow lane interviews the few.
Per-query cascade cost on the toy.
The ANN's top 100 must keep the gold doc or the reranker never sees it.

recall.question: Write the cascade cost formula.
recall.answer: Total = sum over stages of count * cost_each.

recall.question: ANN top 100 at 5 ms, cross-encoder top 20 at 20 ms each. Total? Tightened to top 10?
recall.answer: 405 ms. Tightened: 205 ms.

recall.question: Quality drops though the reranker is great. Where did the gold go?
recall.answer: The funnel dropped it: the ANN's top 100 missed the gold doc.

keyTerms.definition: Guest lectures: not textbooks. The skill is evidence grading.
measured, derived, stated, stale.
Per day for 1000 GPUs at the $3/hour toy price.

recall.question: Name the four evidence grades.
recall.answer: Measured, derived, stated, stale.

recall.question: 1000 GPUs at $3/hour (toy). Daily bill? Useful-day cost at 48% MFU?
recall.answer: $72k/day. Useful-day $150k.

recall.question: The arithmetic checks but the conclusion is wrong. What broke?
recall.answer: The price is stale: a 2022 price quoted in 2024.

keyTerms.definition: Guest evidence is sorted, not swallowed.
Never promote a grade without the artifact.
The future: weight zero in engineering decisions.

recall.question: List the grades in order.
recall.answer: measured > derived > stated > opinion.

recall.question: Grade: '2x faster' with no table; 'O(T d^2)'; 'the future is SSM'.
recall.answer: STATED (do not size a cluster on it); DERIVED (safe for planning); OPINION (weight zero).

recall.question: A team sizes a cluster on a stated claim. What grade did they skip?
recall.answer: Measured: the table, baselines, and seeds.

keyTerms.definition: A proposal: what you will try, what would prove you wrong, what it costs.
Five criteria, 2 points each: question, hypothesis, baselines, budget, failure criteria.
The toy proposal: fails on missing failure criteria.

recall.question: Name the five rubric criteria.
recall.answer: Question, hypothesis, baselines, budget, failure criteria.

recall.question: Scores [2,2,1,2,0]. Total? Fixed version?
recall.answer: 7/10. Add failure criteria: 9/10.

recall.question: The baseline wins in week 2 and the team stalls. What was missing?
recall.answer: Failure criteria: without them the team rationalizes instead of pivoting.

keyTerms.definition: A hypothesis-free profile: you will find something, and it will be wrong.
The toy predicted attention share of the step.
Reports both: 'predicted 62, measured 58'.

recall.question: Define the profiling hypothesis format.
recall.answer: The hypothesis names the suspect, the mechanism, and the predicted number.

recall.question: Predict 62%, measure 58%. Error and verdict?
recall.answer: Error 4 points, under 0.10: the hypothesis survives.

recall.question: The profiler says 12%. What do you do?
recall.answer: Kill the hypothesis: the real suspect (say, dispatch) takes over.

keyTerms.definition: An optimization claim without seeds is a rumor.
The spread the gap must clear.
The minimum unit of evidence.

recall.question: State the minimum evidence rule.
recall.answer: Three seeds minimum: mean plus spread. The claim 'faster' means the gap clears the spread.

recall.question: Losses [2.31, 2.29, 2.33]. Mean, std, verdict vs 2.30?
recall.answer: Mean 2.31, std 0.02. Gap 0.01 < 1 std: no evidence, rejected.

recall.question: Spread is huge. Name two causes.
recall.answer: Mixed GPUs with nondeterministic kernels, or unseeded data ordering.

keyTerms.definition: Speed without a quality gate.
Set from seed noise (C10): here 0.5% > typical noise.

recall.question: Write the gate rule.
recall.answer: Gate: delta >= -epsilon on the task metric.

recall.question: Epsilon -0.5%. A at -0.3%, B at -0.7%, boundary at -0.5%. Verdicts?
recall.answer: A ships, B does not, the boundary case passes.

recall.question: Everything passes the gate but users complain. What is wrong with the metric?
recall.answer: It is a proxy: the gate uses perplexity, the optimization games it, task quality falls.

keyTerms.definition: The defense: on your own work. 'I do not know' is valid; bluffing is not.
Claim, evidence, baseline, failure, cost.
Asks for the baseline you skipped: the poster folds.

recall.question: Name the five defense questions.
recall.answer: Claim, evidence, baseline, failure, cost.

recall.question: Scores [2,2,1,2,1]. Total and gaps?
recall.answer: 8/10. Gaps at baseline and cost.

recall.question: The experiment failed. Can the defense still pass?
recall.answer: Yes: a 10/10 defense with a failed experiment beats an 8/10 with a lucky one.

keyTerms.definition: retrieve -> grade evidence -> propose -> profile -> reproduce -> gate -> defend.
The last stage: the Dec 06 poster session.

recall.question: What is the U10 chapter plate?
recall.answer: The synthesis arc: retrieve to grade evidence to propose to profile to reproduce to gate to defend.

keyTerms.definition: Course-level capstones live in capstones/.
Defend the ANN results against the C12 rubric.

recall.question: What does this unit propose?
recall.answer: Build a toy ANN index, measure the recall/latency curve, then defend the results against the C12 rubric. See lab-10.
